blocks.content: When we compare things, adjectives change their ending. Learn the two endings and you can compare anything clearly.
Add -er to an adjective to compare TWO things: a giraffe is taller than a horse.

steps: A giraffe is taller than a horse.

blocks.prompt: Compare two: A truck is ___ than a car. (big)
blocks.explain: Add -er to compare two things; 'big' doubles the g: bigger.
blocks.rule: Add -er to an adjective to compare two things (double a final consonant after a short vowel).

blocks.content: Add -est to show the most of ALL: the tallest tree in the park.

blocks.prompt: The most of all: That is the ___ mountain of them all. (high)
blocks.explain: Add -est to show the most of all: highest.
blocks.rule: Add -est to an adjective to show the most of all.

blocks.content: Use -er to compare two, and -est for the most of all. For long words, use 'more' and 'most' instead. Let's practise!
